contentHtml:
Ahmedabad: Ahmedabad Police have arrested a 32-year-old pharmacy graduate from the forest region of Pali, Rajasthan, for allegedly stealing 14 iPhones valued at Rs 10.70 lakh from a luxury bus travelling from Pune to Ahmedabad.

The accused has been identified as Gajendrasinh Rajput, who was traced to a relative’s house near the Jawai Leopard Sanctuary in Sumerpur during a joint operation by the Ramol Police and Zone-5 Local Crime Branch (LCB). Police also detained an Ahmedabad resident identified as Mohsin, who allegedly purchased the stolen handsets from Rajput.

During preliminary interrogation, investigators reportedly uncovered an international angle, finding that the stolen phones had been smuggled to Dubai, prompting police to investigate a wider network allegedly involved in moving stolen electronic goods from Gujarat to overseas markets.

The theft reportedly took place on August 15 aboard an overnight luxury bus travelling towards Ahmedabad. A Pune-based mobile dealer, Suresh Thakor, had dispatched a parcel containing 14 iPhones to Salman, a merchant operating a shop on Ashram Road in Ahmedabad. Rajput, who was travelling on the same bus, allegedly noticed the parcel while it was being handed over in Pune.

Police elaborated that he stood nearby pretending to spit and overheard the dealer instructing the bus crew to safeguard the high-value shipment. After learning about the contents of the parcel and the instructions given to the bus staff, Rajput allegedly stole the package during the journey. At the time, he was working at a hospital dispensary in Pune and reportedly earning ₹25,000 per month.

Investigators stated that Rajput subsequently sold the stolen phones to Mohsin and allegedly used the proceeds to fund a stay with his girlfriend at a luxury resort in Udaipur. He also allegedly gifted her one of the stolen iPhones. To avoid detection and tracking, Rajput reportedly deactivated his primary SIM card and cellular data and relied solely on internet-based calls through a Wi-Fi dongle. Acting on specific intelligence about his whereabouts, the Zone-5 LCB team raided his suspected hideout in Pali and recovered ₹8,500 in cash and another iPhone. With this seizure, the immediate recovery in the case reached ₹2.28 lakh.

Police background checks further revealed that Rajput has a previous criminal record, including an offence registered under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act at Himmatnagar Police Station. The Ramol Police are now investigating the entire supply chain through which the stolen electronic devices allegedly moved from local receivers in Gujarat to markets in Dubai.

According to Gujarat Samachar report, the preliminary investigation into the theft revealed that the accused allegedly overheard instructions regarding the valuable parcel, stole the 14 iPhones during the bus journey and later sold them, while the investigation also uncovered the alleged Dubai connection.

Investigators are examining the possible involvement of additional persons in purchasing, transferring and smuggling the stolen iPhones, as the Dubai connection has expanded the scope of the investigation into what police suspect may be a larger international network dealing in stolen electronic goods.
